result.stdout:
Description:
  Run PostgreSQL locally: named instances of any version, SQL, schema, and an MCP server.

Usage:
  pgembed [command] [options]

Options:
  -h, --help  Show help and usage information
  --version   Show version information

Commands:
  versions                   List the Postgres versions published for this platform
  install <version>          Download and extract a Postgres version into the cache
  extensions <version>       List the extensions CREATE EXTENSION can use in a version
  start <name>               Start a named instance in the background (created on first start)
  stop [<names>]             Stop instances cleanly
  kill [<names>]             Force-kill instances (last resort)
  restart <name>             Stop and start an instance with its saved settings
  status [<names>] (list)    Show instances: version, port, process, state, uptime, data size
  connstr <name>             Print an instance's connection string
  logs <name>                Show an instance's server log
  rm [<names>]               Delete instances and their data
  sql [<target>] [<sql>]     Run SQL against an instance and show the results
  format [<sql>]             Format SQL, keeping comments; needs no server
  schema <target> [<table>]  List tables, or describe one: columns, keys, indexes, constraints
  mcp                        Run an MCP server over standard input and output, for AI assistants
  doctor                     Check that Postgres can run here
  cache                      Inspect and clean the download cache

Description:
  List the Postgres versions published for this platform

  Examples:
    pgembed versions
    pgembed versions --major 17

Usage:
  pgembed versions [options]

Options:
  --major <MAJOR>     Every published version of one major, for example 17
  --all               Every published version
  --platform <RID>    Another platform: win-x64, linux-x64, linux-arm64, linux-musl-x64,
                      linux-musl-arm64, osx-x64, osx-arm64
  --refresh           Check for new versions now instead of using the cached list
  --cache-dir <PATH>  Cache folder for downloads and instances (default: PGEMBED_CACHE_DIR, else the
                      per-user cache folder)
  --maven-repo <URL>  Maven repository or mirror with the Postgres binaries (default: Maven Central,
                      or PGEMBED_MAVEN_REPO)
  --json              Machine-readable output
  --verbose           Log details to standard error
  -h, --help          Show help and usage information

Description:
  Start a named instance in the background (created on first start)

  Examples:
    pgembed start app --version 17
    pgembed start ci --version 16,17,18

Usage:
  pgembed start <name> [options]

Arguments:
  <name>  Instance name; with several versions, the prefix: <name>-<major>

Options:
  -v, --version <VERSION>  Version for a new instance (17, 17.6, 17.6.0, latest), or several:
                           16,17,18. Kept for later starts
  -p, --port <PORT>        Port (default: the instance's remembered port, else 5432 if free, else a
                           free port)
  --param <KEY=VALUE>      Postgres setting, for example --param max_connections=300. Repeatable
  --extension <URL>        Extension zip to install; append #sha256=<hex> to verify it. Repeatable
  --password               Require a password for TCP connections, for shared machines: pgembed
                           generates it and keeps it in the instance's private settings; pgembed
                           connstr prints it
  --locale <LOCALE>        Locale for a new instance's data (default: en_US.UTF-8; on Linux without
                           it, C.UTF-8)
  --foreground             Stay attached and stream the log; Ctrl+C stops the server
  --refresh                Check for new versions now
  --cache-dir <PATH>       Cache folder for downloads and instances (default: PGEMBED_CACHE_DIR,
                           else the per-user cache folder)
  --maven-repo <URL>       Maven repository or mirror with the Postgres binaries (default: Maven
                           Central, or PGEMBED_MAVEN_REPO)
  --json                   Machine-readable output
  --verbose                Log details to standard error
  -h, --help               Show help and usage information

result.stdout:
Description:
  Run SQL against an instance and show the results

  Examples:
    pgembed sql app "SELECT version()"
    pgembed sql app -f seed.sql
    pgembed sql --check -f migrate.sql

Usage:
  pgembed sql [<target>] [<sql>] [options]

Arguments:
  <target>  An instance name, or a connection string: Npgsql, postgresql:// URI, libpq key=value or
            JDBC. Not needed with --check
  <sql>     SQL to run; or use -f, or pipe it in. Without any, opens an interactive prompt

Options:
  -f, --file <PATH>   Run a SQL file
  --db <DATABASE>     Database (default: postgres for an instance, else the connection string's)
  --schema <SCHEMA>   Schema for unqualified names (sets the search path)
  --format <FORMAT>   table (fits the terminal; the default there), aligned (psql-style, one row per
                      line; the default when output is redirected), json, csv or markdown
  --max-rows <N>      Rows shown per result in table format (default: 500); other formats return all
  --timing            Show how long each statement took
  --check             Check the syntax and summarize each statement (tables, functions, whether it
                      asks first); needs no server
  --no-pager          Never open a pager (default: a result taller than the terminal opens in
                      PGEMBED_PAGER, PAGER or less -SFX)
  -y, --yes           Run statements that change the schema or existing rows without asking
  --cache-dir <PATH>  Cache folder for downloads and instances (default: PGEMBED_CACHE_DIR, else the
                      per-user cache folder)
  --maven-repo <URL>  Maven repository or mirror with the Postgres binaries (default: Maven Central,
                      or PGEMBED_MAVEN_REPO)
  --json              Machine-readable output
  --verbose           Log details to standard error
  -h, --help          Show help and usage information

  Examples:
    pgembed schema app
    pgembed schema app books
    pgembed schema app orders --schema sales --json

Arguments:
  <target>  An instance name, or a connection string: Npgsql, postgresql:// URI, libpq key=value or
            JDBC
  <table>   A table or view to describe; * and ? describe every match. Without it, lists the tables
            and views

Options:
  --db <DATABASE>     Database (default: postgres for an instance, else the connection string's)
  --schema <SCHEMA>   Only this schema; unqualified table names are looked up in it
  --format <FORMAT>   table (the default in a terminal), aligned (the default when redirected), csv
                      or markdown; --json for structured output
  --cache-dir <PATH>  Cache folder for downloads and instances (default: PGEMBED_CACHE_DIR, else the
                      per-user cache folder)

    pgembed schema app orders --schema sales --json

Usage:
  pgembed schema <target> [<table>] [options]

Arguments:
  <target>  An instance name, or a connection string: Npgsql, postgresql:// URI, libpq key=value or
            JDBC
  <table>   A table or view to describe; * and ? describe every match. Without it, lists the tables
            and views

Options:
  --db <DATABASE>     Database (default: postgres for an instance, else the connection string's)
  --schema <SCHEMA>   Only this schema; unqualified table names are looked up in it
  --format <FORMAT>   table (the default in a terminal), aligned (the default when redirected), csv
                      or markdown; --json for structured output
  --cache-dir <PATH>  Cache folder for downloads and instances (default: PGEMBED_CACHE_DIR, else the
                      per-user cache folder)
  --maven-repo <URL>  Maven repository or mirror with the Postgres binaries (default: Maven Central,
                      or PGEMBED_MAVEN_REPO)
  --json              Machine-readable output
  --verbose           Log details to standard error
  -h, --help          Show help and usage information

Usage:

Options:
  --read-only                            Refuse anything that writes, on every target
  --no-confirm                           Run changes, kills and removals without asking (for
                                         sandboxes and throwaway agents)
  --allow-external-writes                Allow writes to servers pgembed did not start (named
                                         connections and connection strings); read-only otherwise
  --statement-timeout <SECONDS>          Seconds a statement may run before it is cancelled (default
                                         120; 0 for none)

                                         superuser (PostgreSQL 14+): it reads, writes and creates,
                                         but cannot reach files, programs or libraries, even through
                                         functions; it cannot alter tables the superuser owns
  --connection <NAME=CONNECTION_STRING>  A server the assistant can use by name without seeing its
